what_its_for: Exenatide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by helping your pancreas release insulin when your blood sugar is high, slowing down digestion, and reducing the amount of sugar your liver releases. It is not used for type 1 diabetes.
how_to_take: Exenatide comes as a shot (injection) that you give yourself under the skin (subcutaneous injection) in your stomach area, thigh, or upper arm. Byetta is a pen you inject twice a day. Bydureon and Bydureon BCise are extended-release forms you inject once a week. Always follow your doctor or diabetes educator's instructions on how to prepare and inject your dose. Never inject into a vein or muscle. Rotate your injection sites each time to avoid skin problems. Do not share your pen or needles with anyone else.
dosing: Byetta (twice-daily): The usual starting dose is 5 micrograms (mcg) injected twice a day, within 60 minutes BEFORE your morning and evening meals. After about 1 month, your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mcg twice a day. Bydureon / Bydureon BCise (once-weekly): The usual dose is 2 mg injected once a week, on the same day each week, at any time of day, with or without food. Your doctor will tell you exactly which form and dose is right for you.
missed_dose: Byetta (twice-daily): If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regularly scheduled time before your next meal. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Bydureon / Bydureon BCise (once-weekly): If you miss your weekly dose and your next scheduled dose is more than 3 days away, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If your next scheduled dose is in 1 to 2 days, skip the missed dose and resume your regular weekly schedule. Do not take two doses within 3 days of each other.
storage: Byetta pens: Store unused, unopened pens in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F / 2°C to 8°C). Once you start using a pen, you can keep it at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) but use it within 30 days. Do not freeze exenatide — throw it away if it has been frozen. Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Bydureon / Bydureon BCise: Store in the refrigerator. You may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for up to 4 weeks if needed. Protect from light and heat. Always check the expiration date and throw away expired medication safely.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can cause low blood sugar or high blood sugar. Do not take Byetta within 1 hour before a meal (it must be taken before eating, not after). Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or have low blood sugar. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medications you take, because exenatide can slow down how your body absorbs some medicines — for example, take antibiotics or birth control pills at least 1 hour BEFORE your exenatide injection. Avoid injecting into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or lumpy.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: severe stomach pain that does not go away (possibly with vomiting) — this could be a sign of pancreatitis; signs of low blood sugar such as shakiness, sweating, fast heartbeat, dizziness, or confusion; signs of kidney problems such as decreased urination or swelling in your legs; a lump or pain at your injection site that does not go away; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; nausea and vomiting that are severe or do not improve.
when_it_works: Exenatide starts lowering your blood sugar after your first dose. However, it may take several weeks to a few months to see the full effect on your A1C (your 3-month blood sugar average). Many people also notice some weight loss over time. Keep taking your medication even if you feel well — type 2 diabetes often has no symptoms, but good blood sugar control is very important for your long-term health.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Exenatide is generally not recommended during pregnancy. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor about safer options for managing your blood sugar. Kidney disease: Exenatide is not recommended if you have severe kidney disease or are on dialysis. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Elderly patients (65 years and older): Exenatide can be used in older adults, but they may be more sensitive to side effects such as nausea and low blood sugar. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: Exenatide is not approved for use in children or teenagers under 18 years old.
